html:
Paraguay won its independence in a bloodless rising in Asunción on 14 and 15 May 1811, when officers removed the Spanish governor.

A year earlier Buenos Aires had set up its own government and demanded that the provinces obey it. Paraguay refused. An army from Buenos Aires under Manuel Belgrano invaded in 1811 and was beaten by Paraguayan militia. Paraguayans then turned on the Spanish governor, and a junta took power that would not take orders from Spain or from Buenos Aires.

In 1813 a congress declared a republic, and the lawyer José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia soon ruled it alone. Argentina did not recognise Paraguay until 1852. Its independence came within the wider Spanish American wars of independence, but by its own path.
sum: Paraguay won its independence in a bloodless rising in Asunción on 14 and 15 May 1811, when officers removed the Spanish governor.
